newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq postpones a business visit to Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Iraq postpones a business visit to Lebanon.

text.p: Iraq has postponed a visit by a business delegation to Lebanon after Beirut refused to allow Iraqi athletes to participate in the Pan Arab Games, the Iraqi News Agency INA reported on Monday.
"The Iraqi trade and industrial delegation has postponed its visit to Lebanon until an unspecified time," INA quoted a trade ministry source as saying.

It said the delegation was scheduled to leave to Lebanon in August upon an invitation from the Lebanese industries federation. A team of Lebanese businessmen is scheduled to travel to Baghdad in early August.
The 97 Iraqi athletes returned back home on Monday, a source at the Iraqi National Olympics Committee said. Iraqi newspapers said Syria hosted the Iraqi athletes in Damascus while on their way home.
"Our athletes have arrived safe today afternoon aboard three buses," the source told Reuters.

The Iraqi athletes, stranded for two days at the Lebanese border, headed home on Saturday after Beirut refused to grant them visas to take part in the games which opened in the Lebanese capital on Saturday night.
The row over the games appears to have derailed efforts by the two countries to resume diplomatic ties which were cut in 1994 after the murder of an Iraqi dissident in Beirut.
Over the last three months both countries have been exchanging trade teams and their officials have hinted they were willing to resume political and economic ties.
On Thursday Iraq and Lebanon signed an agreement to hold a trade exhibition in Baghdad in September. INA did not say whether that exhibition was also called off.
Iraqi media has been harshly attacking Lebanon for not granting visas for the Iraqi athletes.
